mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy that lowers the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points within one month signals aggressive monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate and increase in nonfarm payrolls signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong housing market activity (HOUST above 650 thousand units), the construction sector and related consumer spending boost economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST > 650, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A reading of industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (the 2017 base year index) indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate profit expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A low rate of consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL below 2.5% annually) signals stable price conditions that support corporate profit margins and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL < 2.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS both increase, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of manufacturing slowdown (INDPRO below 95 for two consecutive months), the contraction in industrial output reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 95 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
